segments.he:
תּוֹרָה קסב
עַל־יְדֵי עֲנָוָה שֶׁהוּא אַיִן מַמָּשׁ, עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה יִזְכֶּה לְתוֹרָה וּגְדֻלָּה בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, אֲבָל בְּלֹא זֶה קָשֶׁה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם יַחַד תּוֹרָה וּגְדֻלָּה:
segments.en: But through melancholy and sadness — the mind and knowledge are in exile — and it is difficult to settle one's mind to return to Hashem Yisborach. It is found that sadness is a very great obstacle to the service of Hashem Yisborach. And through joy one becomes a free person — and goes out from the exile — in the aspect of: "for in joy shall you go out" [Isaiah 55:12]. And in the opposite direction — through exile — the mind is not settled — as our Sages said [Megillah 12b] about the children of Ammon and Moav: "their mind was settled because they did not go into exile" — as it is stated [Jeremiah 48:11]: "Moav has been at ease" etc. "and he has not gone into exile — therefore his taste remains in him" etc.
